tasks.title: Verify LXD is installed
tasks.instructions:
Check that LXD is installed on your system by running:

```bash
lxd --version
```

If LXD is not installed, install it with:

```bash
sudo snap install lxd
```

Then add your user to the lxd group (if not already):

```bash
sudo usermod -aG lxd "$USER"
newgrp lxd
```
hints: If you get 'command not found', LXD is not installed. Run `sudo snap install lxd`.
After adding yourself to the lxd group, you may need to log out and back in for it to take effect.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxd --version
# If not installed:
# sudo snap install lxd
# sudo usermod -aG lxd "$USER"
# newgrp lxd
```

tasks.title: Initialize LXD
tasks.instructions:
Initialize LXD with a minimal configuration:

```bash
lxd init --minimal
```

If LXD is already initialized, this command may ask if you want to reconfigure. You can skip if it's already set up.

Verify it's working:

```bash
lxc list
```

You should see an empty table with no errors.
hints: If you get a permission error, make sure you're in the lxd group. Run `newgrp lxd` or re-open your terminal.
lxd init --minimal uses sensible defaults — no need to answer interactive prompts.

tasks.title: Launch your first container
tasks.instructions:
Launch an Ubuntu 24.04 container named `first`:

```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 first
```

This will download the image (may take a minute on first run) and start the container.

Verify it's running:

```bash
lxc list
```

You should see `first` in the RUNNING state.
hints: The first launch downloads the image from the ubuntu: remote server — it takes longer than subsequent launches.
If the download is slow, be patient. The image is cached for future use.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 first
lxc list
```

tasks.title: Create a stopped container
tasks.instructions:
Create a second container named `second` without starting it:

```bash
lxc init ubuntu:24.04 second
```

Then list your instances:

```bash
lxc list
```

You should see `first` RUNNING and `second` STOPPED.
hints: lxc init creates but does not start the instance.
Since the image is already cached from task-3, this should be much faster.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc init ubuntu:24.04 second
lxc list
```

tasks.title: Start and inspect the second container
tasks.instructions:
Start the `second` container and get detailed information about it:

```bash
lxc start second
lxc info second
```

The `lxc info` command shows architecture, PID, resource usage, network config, and more.
hints: lxc start <name> starts a stopped instance.
lxc info <name> gives much more detail than lxc list.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc start second
lxc info second
```
